points.description: States that a stack is a data structure (or abstract data type/collection) that stores elements. Equivalent wording such as 'a structure/container for holding items' earns the mark.

States the ordering property: the last item added is the first to be removed, i.e. last-in-first-out (LIFO). Equivalent wording such as 'the most recently added element is removed first' earns the mark. Naming LIFO alone is sufficient.

rubric.notes: Full marks (5) for a answer that gives both a data structure storing elements and the last-in-first-out removal order, in any equivalent wording. Award P1 alone for a correct data-structure statement with no ordering property, and P2 alone for an ordering description that does not identify a data structure. Nothing else in the model answer carries marks; the LRB/RRB bracket is just formatting.
